passage.title: 月亮宝石
passage.author: Wilkie Collins
passage.text: I was born with a caul, which was advertised for sale, in the newspapers, at the low price of fifteen guineas. I was present myself, and I remember to have felt quite uncomfortable and confused, at a part of myself being disposed of in that way. It is a fact which will be long remembered as remarkable down there, that she was never drowned, but died triumphantly in bed, at ninety-two. It was in vain to represent to her that some conveniences, tea perhaps included, resulted from this objectionable practice. She always returned, with greater emphasis and with an instinctive knowledge of the strength of her objection, 'Let us have no meandering.' My father's eyes had closed upon the light of this world six months, when mine opened on it. An aunt of my father's, and consequently a great-aunt of mine, of whom I shall have more to relate by and by, was the principal magnate of our family.
